# For the Animals: An Argument Guide

> The 213 arguments in the catalogue, with the phrase, the main flaw and the address of the answer. Families in order; DIR codes challenge the moral core and IND codes discuss health, the environment, the economy or who defends veganism.

## A. Sentience and moral status (Part DIR)

Do animals count morally?

- [A1. Animals aren't rational](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-arent-rational.html): Rationality isn't what makes suffering matter, and the criterion would exclude humans who lack it
- [A2. Humans are superior, so we can use the inferior](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/humans-are-superior-so-we-can-use-the-inferior.html): Superior abilities give no right to dominate
- [A3. Animals don't have language](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-dont-have-language.html): An irrelevant criterion for pain; it excludes babies and non-verbal people
- [A4. Animals don't have souls](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-dont-have-souls.html): An unfalsifiable premise used as a public criterion
- [A5. Animals aren't conscious and don't feel pain like we do](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-arent-conscious-and-dont-feel-pain-like-we-do.html): Contradicts the neuroscientific evidence (Cambridge Declaration, 2012; New York Declaration, 2024)
- [A6. Fish and invertebrates don't feel pain](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/fish-and-invertebrates-dont-feel-pain.html): Growing evidence of sentience in fish, cephalopods and decapods
- [A7. No duties, no rights](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/no-duties-no-rights.html): Confuses moral agents with moral patients; it would exclude children
- [A8. Animals aren't persons](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-arent-persons.html): A persuasive definition: pick the concept that excludes them, then conclude they are excluded
- [A9. Rights are a human invention, only for humans](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/rights-are-a-human-invention-only-for-humans.html): Genetic fallacy: where a norm came from doesn't set how far it reaches
- [A10. They're just animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/theyre-just-animals.html): Explicit speciesism: species membership as a moral criterion, like race in racism
- [A11. It's normal for humans to be rational](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-normal-for-humans-to-be-rational.html): Treats individuals by what others have, not by what they have
- [A12. Human babies have the potential to be rational](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/human-babies-have-the-potential-to-be-rational.html): Potential doesn't confer the rights of the actual, and it doesn't cover humans without potential
- [A13. It's natural to put our own first](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-natural-to-put-our-own-first.html): Partiality lets us prefer our own; it does not let us exploit others
- [A14. Plants feel too](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/plants-feel-too.html): No nervous system and no evidence of experience; and if they did feel, animal farming kills more plants
- [A15. Where do you draw the line? Insects? Bacteria?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/where-do-you-draw-the-line-insects-bacteria.html): Continuum fallacy: a fuzzy boundary doesn't erase clear cases
- [A16. Killing without pain isn't harm](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/killing-without-pain-isnt-harm.html): Death takes away good future experiences; the same holds for humans with no sense of time
- [A17. Animals are property](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-are-property.html): Describes a legal status; doesn't justify it (as with slavery)
- [A18. What matters is the species, not the individual](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-matters-is-the-species-not-the-individual.html): Species don't feel; individuals do
- [A19. Vegans anthropomorphize animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-anthropomorphize-animals.html): Denying similar mental states is also an error (anthropodenial), and the evidence contradicts it
- [A20. Humans have intrinsic value; animals have instrumental value](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/humans-have-intrinsic-value-animals-have-instrumental-value.html): Circular: it assumes the conclusion
- [A21. I respect animals, but humans come first](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-respect-animals-but-humans-come-first.html): A special status no one explains and that wouldn't pass the veil of ignorance: the weight should depend on the size of the harm, not on species
- [A22. Humans suffer more than animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/humans-suffer-more-than-animals.html): Suffering more in some cases doesn't license ignoring those who suffer less; and less cognition often means more suffering and more vulnerability
- [A23. Morality exists to protect us from each other](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/morality-exists-to-protect-us-from-each-other.html): It would also exclude babies and vulnerable people; and explaining where a practice came from does not justify it
- [A24. Species is biology, race is a social construct](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/species-is-biology-race-is-a-social-construct.html): A biological criterion can be as unjust as a social one: what makes discrimination unjust is giving someone's interests biased weight
- [A25. Animals don't know they're going to die, so killing them is fine](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-dont-know-theyre-going-to-die-so-killing-them-is-fine.html): What's bad about death is what it takes, not the fear of it: the same reasoning would allow killing babies, people with dementia or people who are asleep

## B. Harm, death and welfare (Part DIR)

Does killing without suffering harm the individual?

- [B1. There is humane slaughter](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/there-is-humane-slaughter.html): A contradiction in terms: there is no compassionate way to kill someone who does not want to die
- [B2. Free-range animals are happy](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/free-range-animals-are-happy.html): They're still killed young; labels have little to do with practice, and changing the scale doesn't change the act
- [B4. The problem is the industry, not consumers](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-problem-is-the-industry-not-consumers.html): The industry exists to meet demand: system and consumer sustain each other
- [B5. They had a good life and a quick death](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/they-had-a-good-life-and-a-quick-death.html): A good life doesn't license taking it; the idea is absurd applied to dogs or humans
- [B6. Without farming, these animals wouldn't even exist](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/without-farming-these-animals-wouldnt-even-exist.html): Bringing someone into existence gives no right to kill them
- [B7. Milk and eggs don't kill anyone](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/milk-and-eggs-dont-kill-anyone.html): Male chicks and calves are discarded, and cows and hens are slaughtered when production drops
- [B8. The law guarantees animal welfare](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-law-guarantees-animal-welfare.html): Laws allow confinement, mutilations without anesthesia and the killing of newborns
- [B9. Those videos are exceptions or staged](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/those-videos-are-exceptions-or-staged.html): Much of what they show is standard, legal industry practice
- [B10. Stressed animals make bad meat, so farmers take good care of them](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/stressed-animals-make-bad-meat-so-farmers-take-good-care-of-them.html): The incentive is small and partial; it doesn't cover suffering that doesn't affect profit

## C. Nature, biology and evolution (Part DIR)

Is what is natural justified?

- [C1. It's natural to eat meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-natural-to-eat-meat.html): Appeal to nature: natural doesn't mean right
- [C2. Lions eat other animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/lions-eat-other-animals.html): Lions aren't moral agents and have no alternative
- [C3. We have canine teeth; we are omnivores](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-have-canine-teeth-we-are-omnivores.html): Being able to eat it isn't needing to; anatomy creates no duty
- [C4. We're at the top of the food chain](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/were-at-the-top-of-the-food-chain.html): Ecologically false (the average human trophic level is about 2.2) and morally irrelevant
- [C5. Eating meat made us evolve](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/eating-meat-made-us-evolve.html): An adaptive past doesn't dictate present morality
- [C6. Might makes right](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/might-makes-right.html): Social Darwinism: it describes a process, not a norm
- [C7. It's the circle of life](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-the-circle-of-life.html): A euphemism: breeding, confining and slaughtering is an industry, not a natural cycle
- [C8. If we don't eat them, animals will take over the planet](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-we-dont-eat-them-animals-will-take-over-the-planet.html): Gets the cause backwards: there are so many because they're bred
- [C9. Farm animals exist for this](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/farm-animals-exist-for-this.html): An imposed purpose: the "function" is assigned by whoever profits
- [C10. Cows need to be milked](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/cows-need-to-be-milked.html): Only because they were made pregnant and bred for overproduction
- [C11. We naturally crave meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-naturally-crave-meat.html): A learned and reinforced preference; desire is no justification
- [C12. We are animals and part of the ecosystem; no one lives without impact](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-are-animals-and-part-of-the-ecosystem-no-one-lives-without-impact.html): Nirvana fallacy and appeal to nature: "harm can't be brought to zero" doesn't mean "it makes no difference how much harm I cause", and "conscious" describes the one who kills, not what happens to the one who dies

## D. Tradition, culture and religion (Part DIR)

Does custom justify it?

- [D1. We've always done it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/weve-always-done-it.html): Appeal to tradition: the same phrase defended slavery and the subjugation of women
- [D2. It's cultural; criticizing it is ethnocentric](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-cultural-criticizing-it-is-ethnocentric.html): Selective cultural relativism: not applied to practices the person condemns
- [D3. Indigenous and traditional peoples eat animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/indigenous-and-traditional-peoples-eat-animals.html): Uses those with no alternative to justify those who have one; veganism already says "as far as is possible and practicable"
- [D4. God gave us dominion over animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/god-gave-us-dominion-over-animals.html): Many traditions read dominion as stewardship; and it is a theological premise, not a public one
- [D5. Jesus ate fish](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/jesus-ate-fish.html): Appeal to authority; a historical context of necessity doesn't carry over
- [D6. Everybody eats meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/everybody-eats-meat.html): Appeal to popularity: popular isn't right
- [D7. It's legal; the law allows it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-legal-the-law-allows-it.html): Legalistic fallacy: the law follows morality, with a delay
- [D8. Barbecues bring the family together](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/barbecues-bring-the-family-together.html): The bond is the gathering, not the animal
- [D9. My grandparents ate meat and lived to 90](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-grandparents-ate-meat-and-lived-to-90.html): Anecdotal evidence and survivorship bias
- [D10. Great thinkers ate meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/great-thinkers-ate-meat.html): Appeal to authority; many also defended human hierarchies we now reject
- [D11. My religion approves of eating animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-religion-approves-of-eating-animals.html): Permitting is not requiring, and religious traditions themselves forbid unnecessary suffering, which today's production causes on a massive scale
- [D12. I'll pay for my mistakes in my next life](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ill-pay-for-my-mistakes-in-my-next-life.html): The phrase admits the wrong and postpones the bill, but the animal pays now; the traditions of karma teach non-violence
- [D13. I don't want to dishonor my parents and my ancestors](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-want-to-dishonor-my-parents-and-my-ancestors.html): Confuses honoring people with repeating what they did: every generation revises earlier practices, and judging a practice is not condemning those who followed it

## E. Relativism, freedom and evasions (Part DIR)

Is it just a matter of choice?

- [E1. It's my personal choice; don't impose your morals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-my-personal-choice-dont-impose-your-morals.html): Personal choice ends where there is a victim; every rule against harm "imposes"
- [E2. Morality is relative](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/morality-is-relative.html): Self-refuting and applied selectively; it confuses taste with a claim about harm to others
- [E4. The state can't ban what I eat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-state-cant-ban-what-i-eat.html): Switches from "is it wrong?" to "should it be banned?"
- [E5. Everything in moderation](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/everything-in-moderation.html): False middle ground: moderation doesn't make an unjustifiable harm acceptable
- [E6. Nobody's perfect; I do what I can](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/nobodys-perfect-i-do-what-i-can.html): True in general, but used to avoid doing what is easy
- [E7. I don't want to see those videos](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-want-to-see-those-videos.html): Willful ignorance: avoiding the information to avoid the obligation
- [E8. I love animals, but...](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-love-animals-but.html): A contradiction between stated values and practice (the meat paradox)
- [E9. Eating meat isn't an ideology; veganism is](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/eating-meat-isnt-an-ideology-veganism-is.html): The dominant norm is invisible to those who follow it (carnism, Joy 2009)
- [E10. Veganism is opinion, not science](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-opinion-not-science.html): No moral position is "just science", including eating meat
- [E11. Even philosophers don't agree](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/even-philosophers-dont-agree.html): Disagreement isn't a tie; there is strong convergence against factory farming
- [E12. I know it's wrong, but I won't change](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-know-its-wrong-but-i-wont-change.html): Admitted weakness of will: concedes the moral point and refuses its consequence
- [E13. Defending animals is just utilitarianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/defending-animals-is-just-utilitarianism.html): Equal consideration is a formal principle accepted by rival theories; knocking down utilitarianism doesn't rescue speciesism
- [E14. He eats meat, but he's a good person](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/he-eats-meat-but-hes-a-good-person.html): Confuses judging the person with judging the act: good people also take part in injustices that custom accepts
- [E15. I admire you, but I can't do it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-admire-you-but-i-cant-do-it.html): Admiring already means agreeing with the moral point; hard is not impossible, and changing gradually, with support, works
- [E16. AIs say that not being vegan isn't wrong](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ais-say-that-not-being-vegan-isnt-wrong.html): Appeal to authority and, at second hand, to the majority: AI repeats the texts it was trained on and is tuned not to take sides; abstaining is not concluding that it isn't wrong

## F. Edge cases and hypotheticals (Part DIR)

What about the desert island?

- [F1. On a desert island, would you eat an animal?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/on-a-desert-island-would-you-eat-an-animal.html): Extreme necessity doesn't justify the practice in normal conditions
- [F2. If a dog and a child were drowning, which would you save?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-a-dog-and-a-child-were-drowning-which-would-you-save.html): A preference in a tragic conflict doesn't license exploiting those who aren't in one
- [F3. So should we stop lions from hunting?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/so-should-we-stop-lions-from-hunting.html): Wild animal suffering is a serious question, and it does not favor eating animals
- [F4. What about the insects you kill while driving?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-about-the-insects-you-kill-while-driving.html): Accidental, unavoidable harm differs from intentional, avoidable harm
- [F6. What about the eggs from my rescued hen?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-about-the-eggs-from-my-rescued-hen.html): A rare, debatable case with no link to the industry; it doesn't legitimize buying
- [F7. Oysters and mussels don't feel](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/oysters-and-mussels-dont-feel.html): Partly plausible; it confirms that sentience is the criterion
- [F8. What about meat that gets thrown away?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-about-meat-that-gets-thrown-away.html): Eating without creating demand is a different case; it still reinforces seeing animals as food
- [F9. You also kill mosquitoes and rats at home](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/you-also-kill-mosquitoes-and-rats-at-home.html): Self-defense and real conflict differ from breeding animals to eat
- [F10. Would you eat an animal that died of natural causes?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/would-you-eat-an-animal-that-died-of-natural-causes.html): No one was killed, so the moral problem is much smaller; but that meat never reaches the market, and refusing to eat a body can be respect, as we do with humans
- [F11. What if they discover that plants feel?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-if-they-discover-that-plants-feel.html): Even in that scenario, eating plants would cause less harm, because animals eat far more plants; not being able to reach zero harm doesn't make everything equivalent

## G. Health and nutrition (Part IND)

Do we need animal products?

- [G1. We need animal protein](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-need-animal-protein.html): Protein needs are met by legumes, grains and soy
- [G2. Plant protein is incomplete](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/plant-protein-is-incomplete.html): A 1970s myth; variety over the day provides all the essential amino acids
- [G3. If you need B12 supplements, it isn't natural](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-you-need-b12-supplements-it-isnt-natural.html): Farm animals also get supplemented B12; and natural is not the criterion (C1)
- [G4. You'll lack iron, zinc and other micronutrients](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/youll-lack-iron-zinc-and-other-micronutrients.html): Plannable with a varied diet; iron deficiency is also common in meat eaters
- [G5. Milk is necessary for your bones](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/milk-is-necessary-for-your-bones.html): Calcium is found in plants and fortified foods
- [G6. Only fish provides omega-3](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/only-fish-provides-omega-3.html): Fish get their DHA from algae, a direct source available to us
- [G7. Soy causes female hormones and cancer](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/soy-causes-female-hormones-and-cancer.html): Phytoestrogens aren't estrogen; meta-analyses don't support the myth
- [G8. Children and pregnant women can't be vegan](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/children-and-pregnant-women-cant-be-vegan.html): Major nutrition bodies consider it appropriate at every life stage, with planning
- [G9. Athletes need meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/athletes-need-meat.html): There are elite vegan athletes; adequate protein intake is what matters
- [G10. I know someone who got sick being vegan](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-know-someone-who-got-sick-being-vegan.html): Anecdotal evidence; it confuses a badly planned diet with a vegan diet
- [G11. My body can't adapt](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-body-cant-adapt.html): The blood type diet has been refuted; individual complaints are rarely investigated
- [G12. A carnivore, paleo or keto diet is healthiest](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-carnivore-paleo-or-keto-diet-is-healthiest.html): Weak, short-term evidence that contradicts the large cohort studies
- [G13. The WHO exaggerates; red meat isn't bad for you](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-who-exaggerates-red-meat-isnt-bad-for-you.html): Cherry picking against the consensus (IARC: processed meat Group 1, red meat Group 2A)
- [G14. Ultra-processed vegan foods are worse than meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ultra-processed-vegan-foods-are-worse-than-meat.html): False dichotomy: veganism doesn't require ultra-processed foods
- [G15. Plants have antinutrients](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/plants-have-antinutrients.html): Doses and preparation make them irrelevant; populations eating plant-based diets live longer
- [G16. Vegans are weak, pale and depressed](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-weak-pale-and-depressed.html): A stereotype; the existing correlations have uncertain or reverse causation
- [G17. My doctor told me to eat meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-doctor-told-me-to-eat-meat.html): An appeal to individual authority against institutional positions
- [G18. Fruitarianism isn't healthy, so veganism isn't either](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/fruitarianism-isnt-healthy-so-veganism-isnt-either.html): Veganism isn't fruitarianism: an all-fruit diet is risky, but a varied, planned vegan diet with B12 is considered adequate
- [G19. Veganism is an eating disorder in disguise](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-an-eating-disorder-in-disguise.html): The association exists, but the disorder usually comes before the diet; community vegans show no more signs of disorder, and the cause of a tragedy is the illness

## H. Environment, ecology and agriculture (Part IND)

Is veganism worse for the planet?

- [H1. Vegans' soy is destroying the Amazon](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-soy-is-destroying-the-amazon.html): Most soy becomes animal feed; pasture is the main driver of deforestation
- [H2. Harvests kill animals; vegans kill too](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/harvests-kill-animals-vegans-kill-too.html): Animal farming uses far more cropland (for feed) and land
- [H3. Regenerative grazing sequesters carbon](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/regenerative-grazing-sequesters-carbon.html): Limited, temporary sequestration that cannot scale; it needs more land per calorie
- [H4. Cattle graze where crops can't grow](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/cattle-graze-where-crops-cant-grow.html): Partly true, but that land could be rewilded and produces few calories
- [H5. Cow methane is biogenic; it doesn't count](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/cow-methane-is-biogenic-it-doesnt-count.html): Methane has a strong short-term effect; growing herds increase warming
- [H6. Avocados and almonds use a lot of water](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/avocados-and-almonds-use-a-lot-of-water.html): A selective comparison; per nutrient, animal products lead in water and land use
- [H7. Imported vegan food pollutes in transport](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/imported-vegan-food-pollutes-in-transport.html): Transport is a small share of emissions; what you eat matters more than how far it traveled
- [H8. Local, organic meat is sustainable](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/local-organic-meat-is-sustainable.html): Grass-fed beef usually needs more land and emits as much or more per kilo
- [H9. Agriculture can't work without manure](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/agriculture-cant-work-without-manure.html): Green manures and compost exist; the manure comes from crops grown for feed
- [H10. Sustainable fishing and aquaculture solve it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sustainable-fishing-and-aquaculture-solve-it.html): Bycatch, overfishing and feed made from wild fish; the suffering continues
- [H11. Hunting controls populations](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/hunting-controls-populations.html): It often causes the imbalance it claims to fix; non-lethal methods exist
- [H12. Livestock pollutes little; the problem is fossil fuels](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/livestock-pollutes-little-the-problem-is-fossil-fuels.html): False dichotomy; food systems account for about a third of emissions
- [H13. If meat is sustainable, there's no problem](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-meat-is-sustainable-theres-no-problem.html): Reduces a moral question about victims to an environmental one
- [H14. Eating insects is the sustainable protein of the future](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/eating-insects-is-the-sustainable-protein-of-the-future.html): Trades environmental impact for trillions of probable victims; plant proteins are just as efficient, with no one to suffer
- [H15. What matters is how food is grown, not whether it comes from animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-matters-is-how-food-is-grown-not-whether-it-comes-from-animals.html): False dichotomy: you can choose plants and care about how they are grown; the type of food weighs more than the production method, and none of it answers what happens to the animal
- [H16. Plant monoculture destroys as much as industrial animal farming](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/plant-monoculture-destroys-as-much-as-industrial-animal-farming.html): Most soy and much of the grain feed farmed animals; eating plants reduces agricultural land, and comparing the worst cropland with the best animal farming is unfair

## I. Other uses: testing, clothing, entertainment (Part IND)

And beyond the plate?

- [I1. Animal testing has saved millions of lives](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animal-testing-has-saved-millions-of-lives.html): A benefit doesn't justify using those who can't consent; translational failure rates are high
- [I2. If you take medicine, you can't oppose testing](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-you-take-medicine-you-cant-oppose-testing.html): Tu quoque; testing is required by law, not chosen by the patient
- [I3. Leather is just a byproduct of meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/leather-is-just-a-byproduct-of-meat.html): Profitable byproducts subsidize slaughter
- [I4. Sheep need to be shorn](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sheep-need-to-be-shorn.html): Only because they were bred for excessive wool; mulesing, and slaughter when production ends
- [I5. Bees make extra honey](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/bees-make-extra-honey.html): Honey is the bees' food reserve; honeybees compete with native pollinators
- [I6. Zoos conserve species and educate](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/zoos-conserve-species-and-educate.html): Few of the species kept are endangered or reintroduced
- [I7. Aquariums and dolphin parks are harmless](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/aquariums-and-dolphin-parks-are-harmless.html): Severe captivity for wide-ranging animals with complex social lives
- [I8. Rodeos, bullfights and circuses are culture](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/rodeos-bullfights-and-circuses-are-culture.html): Appeal to tradition (D1) applied to suffering imposed for entertainment
- [I9. Horses like working and being ridden](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/horses-like-working-and-being-ridden.html): A convenient projection by those who benefit
- [I10. In sport fishing the fish is released](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/in-sport-fishing-the-fish-is-released.html): Injury, stress and post-release mortality; pain as a pastime
- [I11. Having a pet is exploitation too, and your cat eats meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/having-a-pet-is-exploitation-too-and-your-cat-eats-meat.html): Adopting and caring differs from breeding to use; cats need nutrients, not meat; and none of this licenses eating animals
- [I12. Trophy hunting funds conservation](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/trophy-hunting-funds-conservation.html): Little money reaches conservation; it uses individuals as tools

## J. Practicality, economy and society (Part IND)

Is it feasible and fair to ask this?

- [J1. Veganism is expensive](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-expensive.html): Beans, rice, grains and vegetables are among the cheapest foods
- [J2. Poor people have no access](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/poor-people-have-no-access.html): A real barrier for some, which doesn't apply to the person objecting; and many cultures have old vegetarian traditions
- [J3. Farmers and slaughterhouse workers would lose their jobs](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/farmers-and-slaughterhouse-workers-would-lose-their-jobs.html): An argument used against every moral reform; transitions can be planned
- [J4. Agriculture is the backbone of the economy](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/agriculture-is-the-backbone-of-the-economy.html): Economic importance is not a moral justification; it ignores subsidies and external costs
- [J5. What would we do with the animals if everyone went vegan?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-would-we-do-with-the-animals-if-everyone-went-vegan.html): A gradual change reduces births; the problem is created by breeding itself
- [J6. There are more important human problems](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/there-are-more-important-human-problems.html): Priority fallacy: eating plants doesn't take time from any other cause
- [J7. Veganism is a political ideology or a globalist agenda](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-a-political-ideology-or-a-globalist-agenda.html): Guilt by association and conspiracy theory; it doesn't assess the argument
- [J9. It's hard; I don't have time](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-hard-i-dont-have-time.html): Initial difficulty isn't impossibility; inconvenience doesn't justify harm
- [J10. Vegan food is bland](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegan-food-is-bland.html): A generalization from unfamiliarity; most spices and many dishes are already plant-based
- [J11. Meat tastes good](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/meat-tastes-good.html): Taste as a justification for killing: no other context accepts this
- [J12. I eat little meat; that's enough](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-eat-little-meat-thats-enough.html): Reducing is better than nothing, but it doesn't justify what is left
- [J13. Eating out, traveling and parties become impossible](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/eating-out-traveling-and-parties-become-impossible.html): Exaggerates the social cost; options keep growing and adapting is quick
- [J14. Fishers and ranchers would lose their identity](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/fishers-and-ranchers-would-lose-their-identity.html): Identity doesn't justify harm to others; it calls for a just transition
- [J15. A vegan world is utopian](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-vegan-world-is-utopian.html): Confuses full, immediate feasibility with a present individual duty
- [J16. My food beats yours](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-food-beats-yours.html): A taunt, not an argument: the pleasure of taste doesn't weigh against someone's life, and much vegan food is the same food as always
- [J17. Look what you're missing](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/look-what-youre-missing.html): Showing the plate doesn't answer the question about who became the plate; temptation doesn't make the act just
- [J18. This is my living; it feeds my family](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/this-is-my-living-it-feeds-my-family.html): Economic dependence explains why change is hard, but it does not make the activity just; the way out is a planned, supported transition
- [J19. Vegans are against farmers](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-against-farmers.html): Treats farming as a single block: veganism opposes breeding and killing animals, not crop growing, which is where vegan food comes from
- [J20. I don't want to feel left out; eating together is how you belong](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-want-to-feel-left-out-eating-together-is-how-you-belong.html): Belonging doesn't require eating the same dish, and the social discomfort of refusing doesn't compare with the cost to the animal
- [J21. Veganism has become big business](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-has-become-big-business.html): Genetic fallacy: a moral position doesn't become false because someone profits from it, and the business of exploiting animals is far bigger
- [J22. Billions of people depend on fish for protein](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/billions-of-people-depend-on-fish-for-protein.html): The FAO figure refers to 20% of animal protein, not of protein needs, and the dependence of some doesn't justify consumption by those who have a choice

## K. Effectiveness and individual responsibility (Part IND)

Does my choice change anything?

- [K1. One person doesn't make a difference](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/one-person-doesnt-make-a-difference.html): Expected-value reasoning: the elasticity is below 1 but positive, and buying less leads to producing less
- [K2. The animal is already dead](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-animal-is-already-dead.html): The purchase pays for restocking, that is, the next death
- [K4. There is no ethical consumption under capitalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/there-is-no-ethical-consumption-under-capitalism.html): A partial truth used to erase huge differences in harm
- [K5. I'll wait for cultivated meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ill-wait-for-cultivated-meat.html): Postpones the duty until it costs nothing
- [K6. Radical veganism pushes people away](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/radical-veganism-pushes-people-away.html): May be a fair point about strategy, but it is neither a moral rebuttal nor a personal excuse
- [K7. I don't kill; I just eat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-kill-i-just-eat.html): Outsourced morality: paying for the act is taking part in it
- [K9. Vegans should fight for laws, not diets](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-should-fight-for-laws-not-diets.html): False dichotomy; personal consistency and political action complement each other
- [K10. Vegans will always be a minority](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-will-always-be-a-minority.html): Being a minority doesn't make something wrong or useless: change begins with a few, each person reduces demand, and animal protection laws change without a vegan majority

## L. Attacks on veganism and vegans (Part IND)

Can the people saying this be trusted?

- [L1. Vegans are annoying and think they are better](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-annoying-and-think-they-are-better.html): Ad hominem: the messenger's behavior doesn't change whether the message is valid
- [L2. Veganism is a cult, a religion](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-a-cult-a-religion.html): A label used to avoid evaluating; veganism rests on public arguments
- [L3. Hitler was a vegetarian](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/hitler-was-a-vegetarian.html): Reductio ad Hitlerum and guilt by association; historically doubtful
- [L4. You use a phone, so you're a hypocrite](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/you-use-a-phone-so-youre-a-hypocrite.html): Tu quoque: someone's inconsistency doesn't make what they say false
- [L5. Veganism isn't 100% cruelty-free](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-isnt-100-cruelty-free.html): Nirvana fallacy: reducing harm doesn't require eliminating it entirely
- [L6. Vegans care more about animals than people](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-care-more-about-animals-than-people.html): False dilemma and generalization; empathy is not a zero-sum resource
- [L7. Comparing animal farming to slavery or the Holocaust is offensive](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/comparing-animal-farming-to-slavery-or-the-holocaust-is-offensive.html): Distinguish structural analogy from moral equivalence; handle with care and sources
- [L8. If vegans eat fake meat, they want meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-vegans-eat-fake-meat-they-want-meat.html): The problem was never the taste; it was the victim
- [L9. I'll eat double to make up for you](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ill-eat-double-to-make-up-for-you.html): An emotional reaction (reactance), not an argument
- [L10. Most vegans give up](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/most-vegans-give-up.html): Difficulty sticking to it says nothing about whether it is right
- [L11. Vegan activists are radicals and extremists](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegan-activists-are-radicals-and-extremists.html): Judging a cause by the methods of a minority
- [L12. Meat is for real men](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/meat-is-for-real-men.html): A gender stereotype; masculinity is neither a moral nor a nutritional criterion
- [L13. Veganism is just a fad diet](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-just-a-fad-diet.html): Confuses an ethical position about not harming animals with a menu chosen for health or looks
- [L14. Vegans are all hippies](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-all-hippies.html): A stereotype and an attack on the person: animals' suffering doesn't depend on the lifestyle of whoever points it out
- [L15. Vegans are crazy; they have mental problems](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-crazy-they-have-mental-problems.html): An attack on the person: the asker's health doesn't change the answer, the link with depression doesn't show cause, and using mental disorders as insults reinforces stigma
- [L16. Raising vegan children is imposing an ideology](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/raising-vegan-children-is-imposing-an-ideology.html): Every family passes values on to its children, and serving meat is also the parents' choice; what matters is caring for the child's health and explaining the reasons
- [L17. Vegans are speciesists too](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-speciesists-too.html): Tu quoque: having a bias doesn't license harming anyone, it calls for correction; and speciesism is the unjustified disregard of interests, not any preference
- [L18. You don't feel empathy for every animal in the world either](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/you-dont-feel-empathy-for-every-animal-in-the-world-either.html): The question isn't empathy: it is limited and biased, and where it fails we use reason and principles, as we do with distant humans
- [L19. There are sexist, racist and transphobic vegans](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/there-are-sexist-racist-and-transphobic-vegans.html): Tu quoque and an attack on the messenger: a vegan's failing in another cause doesn't change what happens to animals, and the same reasoning would bring down any cause
- [L20. Vegan documentaries are manipulated](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegan-documentaries-are-manipulated.html): Generalizes from some films' errors to everything: the footage shows standard, legal practices, and the moral conclusion doesn't depend on any film
- [L21. Vegans treat vegetarians as enemies](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-treat-vegetarians-as-enemies.html): An attack on the messenger: some vegans' hostility is a mistake, but the criticism is of milk and egg production, not of people
- [L22. Vegans think they're the only ones who really defend animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-think-theyre-the-only-ones-who-really-defend-animals.html): Generalizes from some vegans and confuses criticizing an inconsistency with despising people; those who rescue animals already accept that animals matter
- [L23. Vegans defend animals, but they support abortion](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-defend-animals-but-they-support-abortion.html): Tu quoque and generalization: veganism has no position on abortion, the two cases have different structures, and someone's inconsistency wouldn't justify exploiting animals
- [L24. Vegans are racist, because they criticize Afro-Brazilian religions](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-racist-because-they-criticize-afro-brazilian-religions.html): Generalizes the selective criticism of some: the consistent criterion criticizes every avoidable killing of animals, starts with the industry and doesn't pick a people as its target
- [L25. Vegans are against religion](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-against-religion.html): False generalization: there are vegans in every religion, whole traditions teach not harming animals, and veganism is compatible with faith and with the absence of faith
- [L26. Veganism is moral puritanism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-moral-puritanism.html): A label in place of a rebuttal: veganism is about harm to third parties, not the purity of the eater, and every morality goes against natural impulses
- [L27. Sentientists are even crazier than vegans](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-are-even-crazier-than-vegans.html): Attack on the person and appeal to ridicule: strangeness is not error, and the fair test is to apply the same scenario to humans and examine the premise

## M. Ex-vegans: why I gave up (Part IND)

Does having given up change what is right?

- [M1. I stopped being vegan because I started feeling unwell](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-stopped-being-vegan-because-i-started-feeling-unwell.html): The discomfort is real but rarely investigated: it usually comes from eating too little, lack of B12 or poor planning, and can be solved without animal products
- [M2. I stopped being vegan because I'm at a different stage of life](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-stopped-being-vegan-because-im-at-a-different-stage-of-life.html): A stage of life changes what is easy, not what happens to the animals; a hard stage calls for adjustments, not for giving up
- [M3. Being vegan limited me when eating at my relatives' homes](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/being-vegan-limited-me-when-eating-at-my-relatives-homes.html): The social cost is real, but there are ways through: talking beforehand, bringing a dish to share, eating what is already vegan on the table
- [M4. Being vegan is hard if you travel a lot](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/being-vegan-is-hard-if-you-travel-a-lot.html): The difficulty of some meals justifies, at most, a genuine exception, not giving up veganism at home
- [M5. I used to be vegan; I know what I'm talking about](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-used-to-be-vegan-i-know-what-im-talking-about.html): Having been vegan gives experience of how it was for that person, not authority on the moral question
- [M6. Vegans are annoying and bossy; I don't want to be part of that group](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-annoying-and-bossy-i-dont-want-to-be-part-of-that-group.html): Confuses the principle with the group: you can leave hostile people without ceasing to spare animals
- [M7. I don't want to be labeled; the label brings pressure](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-want-to-be-labeled-the-label-brings-pressure.html): Confuses the label with the practice: the name is optional, and what reaches the animals is what one does
- [M8. It became an obsession; I lived with guilt](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/it-became-an-obsession-i-lived-with-guilt.html): False dichotomy between total purity and giving up: veganism asks for what is possible and practicable, not perfection
- [M9. I was vegan for my health, and I changed my mind](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-was-vegan-for-my-health-and-i-changed-my-mind.html): Changing your mind about health does not answer the reason concerning animals, which may have existed and lost strength, or never been examined
- [M10. I was vegan and started getting too radical, too rigid](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-was-vegan-and-started-getting-too-radical-too-rigid.html): The rigidity comes from how veganism is lived, not from the principle; the way can change without giving up the reason concerning animals

## N. Wild animals, new minds and the future (Part DIR)

Should we help, not just stop harming?

- [N1. Wild animals live free and happy](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/wild-animals-live-free-and-happy.html): The adults we see are the exception: in most species, almost all young die shortly after birth, from hunger, cold, disease or predation
- [N2. Suffering and death are part of nature](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/suffering-and-death-are-part-of-nature.html): Diseases are part of human life too, and that was never a reason not to treat them; the harm isn't smaller for the victim because no one is to blame
- [N3. We didn't cause it, so we have no duty to help](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-didnt-cause-it-so-we-have-no-duty-to-help.html): Omission bias: no one would accept this reasoning about a drowning child or flood victims
- [N4. It's impossible to solve suffering in nature; it's too big and complex](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-impossible-to-solve-suffering-in-nature-its-too-big-and-complex.html): Not being able to solve everything is no reason to do nothing: we already vaccinate foxes, rescue animals in disasters, and can research to do more
- [N5. Meddling with nature is wrong; we could make everything worse](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/meddling-with-nature-is-wrong-we-could-make-everything-worse.html): Risk calls for study and caution, as in medicine, not for omission: that is the proposal of welfare biology
- [N6. Who are we to interfere with nature?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/who-are-we-to-interfere-with-nature.html): We interfere all the time, with cities, farming and medicine; and no one calls helping an injured person arrogant
- [N7. A balanced nature is good for animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-balanced-nature-is-good-for-animals.html): Balance measures numbers, not wellbeing; and environmental programmes kill thousands of animals for goals we would never accept for humans
- [N8. Helping wild animals isn't veganism; it's a different cause](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/helping-wild-animals-isnt-veganism-its-a-different-cause.html): If sentience is what matters, suffering doesn't stop counting because we didn't cause it; and one cause doesn't stop us researching the other
- [N9. Machines will never feel; robots and AIs need no rights](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/machines-will-never-feel-robots-and-ais-need-no-rights.html): If an artificial mind ever feels, its substrate matters no more than species does; and uncertainty calls for precaution before creating minds at scale
- [N10. Using medicine and genetics to end suffering is playing God](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/using-medicine-and-genetics-to-end-suffering-is-playing-god.html): We already use anaesthesia, vaccines and painkillers without calling it playing God; the issue is safety and consent, not the natural origin of pain
- [N11. Those not yet born don't matter](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/those-not-yet-born-dont-matter.html): Whoever is born will feel what we leave them: that's why burying toxic waste is wrong, even if the victims don't exist yet
- [N12. That's science fiction; we have real problems now](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/thats-science-fiction-we-have-real-problems-now.html): An uncertain but immense risk can deserve attention, and much of what reduces future suffering, like widening the moral circle, also helps now
- [N13. Sentientists are against preserving species and biodiversity](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-are-against-preserving-species-and-biodiversity.html): Species and biodiversity don't feel: the sentientist supports preservation when it is good for individuals and questions it only when it harms them
- [N14. Sentientists want to get rid of forests](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-want-to-get-rid-of-forests.html): Straw man: the real proposals are research, targeted help and caution, and recognizing that there is suffering in a place isn't proposing to destroy it
- [N15. Sentientists give the same weight to insects, invertebrates and mammals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-give-the-same-weight-to-insects-invertebrates-and-mammals.html): Confuses equal consideration with equal weight: similar interests weigh the same, and each being's weight depends on how much it can feel, which is uncertain but not zero
- [N16. Sentientists defend parasitism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-defend-parasitism.html): Incomplete count: without treatment many parasites die with the host, death is only a harm to those who feel and would have a good life, and preventing is not killing

## Stop saying this

- [V1. Going vegan will make you healthier.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/going-vegan-will-make-you-healthier.html): It's imprecise: any badly planned diet carries risks.
- [V2. Veganism would end world hunger.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/veganism-would-end-world-hunger.html): It ignores that hunger is largely a problem of distribution and political will, not just of farm output.
- [V3. Go vegan for the planet.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/go-vegan-for-the-planet.html): The problem isn't that the environmental argument is false. It's that it is fragile exactly where it most needs to be solid: if the reason to reject animal farming is its environmental impact, cleaner animal farming would solve the problem without solving anything for the animals.
- [V4. Meat eaters are psychopaths.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/meat-eaters-are-psychopaths.html): It's inaccurate and counterproductive. Most of these people have genuine emotional bonds.
- [V5. There's no such thing as an ex-vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/theres-no-such-thing-as-an-ex-vegan.html): Being vegan is an ethical position held up by arguments and repeated choices, not a genetic trait. Any such position can be abandoned. There are ex-abolitionists, ex-feminists and ex-pacifists for the same reason.
- [V6. Using force to protect animals is always wrong.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/using-force-to-protect-animals-is-always-wrong.html): The question is more open than that certainty suggests. Absolute pacifism trips over its own logic: refusing to stop a greater harm, in practice, lets it happen. And we accept forceful intervention for humans who cannot defend themselves, such as a child being attacked.
- [V7. Being vegan is very expensive.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/being-vegan-is-very-expensive.html): Coming from a vegan, the phrase confirms one of the myths most used against veganism, and pushes away people who might join.
- [V8. Anemia mostly affects meat eaters.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anemia-mostly-affects-meat-eaters.html): It's a base-rate fallacy: since most people eat meat, most cases of almost anything occur among meat eaters. That doesn't show that meat causes anemia.
- [V9. Every nutrition body in the world approves vegan diets for everyone.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/every-nutrition-body-in-the-world-approves-vegan-diets-for-everyone.html): It overstates the consensus. The US Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and the British Dietetic Association say well-planned vegan diets can be appropriate at every stage of life. But the German Nutrition Society, in 2024, neither recommended nor advised against vegan diets for pregnant women, children and older adults, for lack of data, and European pediatric bodies are cautious.
- [V10. Doctors don't know anything about nutrition.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/doctors-dont-know-anything-about-nutrition.html): It's a generalization. Nutrition training in medical school is often short, but that doesn't mean no doctor understands the subject, and many specialize in it.
- [V11. In India almost everyone is vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/in-india-almost-everyone-is-vegan.html): It confuses vegetarianism with veganism. About 39% of Indian adults say they are vegetarian, and milk consumption in the country is very high.
- [V12. Each vegan saves 200 animals a year.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/each-vegan-saves-200-animals-a-year.html): The number looks precise, but it's a simple division: total animals killed divided by the number of people. It ignores that production doesn't fall in the same proportion as demand, because prices drop and others buy part of what was not bought.
- [V13. Hitler wasn't even really a vegetarian.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/hitler-wasnt-even-really-a-vegetarian.html): Hitler's diet is debated by historians, and answering on historical grounds unintentionally accepts that it would matter to the discussion.
- [V14. All animals are slaughtered fully conscious, without stunning.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/all-animals-are-slaughtered-fully-conscious-without-stunning.html): It's a generalization. In the European Union and in Brazil, the law requires stunning cattle, pigs and poultry before bleeding, and in the United States federal law requires it for mammals, though not for poultry. Most slaughter follows these rules, even with failures and exceptions.
- [V15. Jesus was a vegetarian.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/jesus-was-a-vegetarian.html): The Gospels describe Jesus eating and offering fish, and the theories that he was vegetarian, for example through a link with the Essenes, have no solid historical basis.
- [V16. Great geniuses like Einstein and Da Vinci were vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/great-geniuses-like-einstein-and-da-vinci-were-vegan.html): It's the same appeal to authority as the opposing argument, just from the other side. If the diet of famous thinkers doesn't prove that eating meat is right, it doesn't prove that not eating it is either.
- [V17. Non-vegans are our enemies, and hating them is normal.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/non-vegans-are-our-enemies-and-hating-them-is-normal.html): Almost every vegan was once a non-vegan. People who eat animals today are, in general, where we used to be: repeating a habit learned in childhood, without ever having stopped to examine it. Treating them as enemies is treating who we were as an enemy.
- [V18. Every vegan has to be friendly with non-vegans, or we won't convince anyone.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/every-vegan-has-to-be-friendly-with-non-vegans-or-we-wont-convince.html): There is a lot of truth here: hostile conversations tend to produce defensiveness and rejection, and someone who feels attacked stops listening. Treating the person with respect helps.
- [V19. We have to confront non-vegans, since they're the extremists.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/we-have-to-confront-non-vegans-since-theyre-the-extremists.html): Part of the sentence has a basis: confronting an unjust practice is legitimate, and thinking it wrong to kill animals needlessly is not an extreme position.
- [V20. God didn't make animals for humans.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/god-didnt-make-animals-for-humans.html): Religious arguments of this kind depend on belief, not on reasons anyone can share, so they don't persuade people of a different faith.
- [V21. We should love animals.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/we-should-love-animals.html): It confuses affection with respect. No one is obliged to love humans or animals, but no one has the right to harm them for that reason.
- [V22. Humans come first.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/humans-come-first.html): As a general principle, it is plain speciesism, whether applied by vegans or non-vegans.
- [V23. I'm vegan out of compassion for all living beings.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/im-vegan-out-of-compassion-for-all-living-beings.html): Veganism's criterion isn't being alive, it's being sentient. Plants, fungi and single-celled organisms are alive, but there's no evidence they can be harmed in the sense that matters.
- [V24. Pigs are smarter than a three-year-old child.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/pigs-are-smarter-than-a-three-year-old-child.html): The comparison is widely shared but rests on weak studies. The experiment in which pigs used a mirror to find food has not been replicated, and comparing the intelligence of species by a single measure has no solid basis.
- [V25. Comparing it to slavery pushes people away.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/comparing-it-to-slavery-pushes-people-away.html): It can look like a strategic concern. The test is simple: if it were shown that the comparison is more effective at improving the situation of animals, would you start supporting it? If the answer is no, the objection was always moral, just dressed up as tactics.
- [V26. Don't show the footage; it's too shocking.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/dont-show-the-footage-its-too-shocking.html): At some point this caution becomes an inverted priority: it treats the discomfort of the viewer as more important than the suffering of those being filmed.
- [V27. This partial law is unfair to the other animals.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/this-partial-law-is-unfair-to-the-other-animals.html): It sounds like an even stronger commitment, but it proves too much: since it's impossible to ban every form of exploitation at once, someone who cares about outcomes would prefer a real reduction in suffering to none.
- [V28. Not your mom, not your milk.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/not-your-mom-not-your-milk.html): It's an appeal to nature: it suggests milk from another species is wrong because nature didn't reserve it for us. Natural doesn't define right, and vegans point out this same mistake in "it's natural to eat meat".
- [V29. Eggs are chicken periods.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/eggs-are-chicken-periods.html): Even if the comparison were accurate, it says nothing moral. Being gross doesn't make something wrong, and not being gross wouldn't make it right. The listener can simply say they don't care.
- [V30. No adult animal drinks milk.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/no-adult-animal-drinks-milk.html): It's an appeal to nature. We do many things no other animal does, like cooking, and that doesn't make them wrong; other animals not drinking milk doesn't make milk wrong either.
- [V31. Meat eaters eat more soy than vegans.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/meat-eaters-eat-more-soy-than-vegans.html): It's true that about three quarters of the world's soy becomes animal feed, and that is a good argument about deforestation.
- [V32. In a room with a rabbit and an apple, a child eats the apple and plays with the rabbit.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/in-a-room-with-a-rabbit-and-an-apple-a-child-eats-the-apple-and-plays.html): It's an appeal to nature: it suggests that what is right is what a child would do by instinct. Natural doesn't define right, and vegans point out this same mistake in "it's natural to eat meat". If children had the urge to bite the rabbit, that would not make it just to kill it.
- [V33. Cats can't be vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/cats-cant-be-vegan.html): Many vegans repeat this as if it were established fact, but the available evidence points the other way. In a study of 1,369 cats published in PLOS ONE in 2023, the 127 fed a vegan diet tended to be as healthy or healthier on all seven general indicators, and a 2021 study of more than a thousand cats in Canada and the US also found no harm. A vegan cat food tested at the Federal University of Lavras, in Brazil, met the cats' needs on the measures assessed.
- [V34. Humans are biologically herbivores.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/humans-are-biologically-herbivores.html): It isn't an ethical argument. It suggests we should be vegan because we can't make use of meat, milk and eggs, not because exploiting animals is wrong.
- [V35. Vegans are sexier and better in bed.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/vegans-are-sexier-and-better-in-bed.html): It takes the focus off the animals and appeals to the listener's self-interest.
- [V36. Broccoli and spinach have more protein than meat.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/broccoli-and-spinach-have-more-protein-than-meat.html): The confusion comes from charts that count protein per calorie, not per weight. About half of spinach's calories come from protein, but it has very few calories: 100 g provides only about 3 g of protein.
- [V37. Vegans don't need to supplement B12.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/vegans-dont-need-to-supplement-b12.html): It is irresponsible and can put people's health at risk. Calling supplementation "a pharmaceutical industry scam" is a conspiracy claim with no evidence.
- [V38. Gorillas, bulls and horses get strong eating only plants.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/gorillas-bulls-and-horses-get-strong-eating-only-plants.html): It's a false analogy. Cattle digest grass with the help of microbes in the rumen, and horses ferment fiber in the large intestine; the microbes turn fiber and other compounds into nutrients, including protein. Gorillas spend much of the day eating large volumes of leaves and have a gut adapted to ferment them. The human digestive system doesn't work like that.
- [V39. All the B12 in meat comes from supplements.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/all-the-b12-in-meat-comes-from-supplements.html): It's an exaggeration. Farmed pigs and chickens get B12 in their feed, but in cattle B12 is produced by bacteria in the rumen from cobalt, which doesn't always need to be added.
- [V40. Livestock pollutes more than all cars, planes and ships combined.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/livestock-pollutes-more-than-all-cars-planes-and-ships-combined.html): The phrase comes from the 2006 FAO report, which compared livestock's 18% of emissions with about 13% for transport. But the accounting differed: for livestock it counted the whole chain, from feed to slaughter; for transport, only fuel combustion. One of the authors acknowledged the problem in 2010.
- [V41. Livestock causes 51% of the world's greenhouse gas emissions.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/livestock-causes-51-of-the-worlds-greenhouse-gas-emissions.html): The figure comes from a 2009 piece published by the Worldwatch Institute, which counted, for example, animal respiration, something international methodologies do not count as emissions. It became famous through the documentary *Cowspiracy*.
- [V42. Animal testing is useless: 90% of drugs fail.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/animal-testing-is-useless-90-of-drugs-fail.html): It's an exaggeration. About 90% of drug candidates fail in human trials, and species differences are one of the causes. But failures have many other causes, and the figure doesn't prove that tests have never helped.
- [V43. Unseasoned meat tastes of nothing; all the flavor comes from seasoning.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/unseasoned-meat-tastes-of-nothing-all-the-flavor-comes-from-seasoning.html): It's an exaggeration. Meat has its own flavor, which comes from fat, from compounds like heme iron and from the reactions that happen when it browns.
- [V44. It's proven that vegans are more empathetic.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/its-proven-that-vegans-are-more-empathetic.html): The claim usually relies on a 2010 neuroimaging study of 60 people, which measured brain activation in response to images, not behavior. It is modest evidence, not proof.
- [V45. Koko the gorilla held conversations in sign language.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/koko-the-gorilla-held-conversations-in-sign-language.html): Koko learned many signs, but the claim that she used a language, with grammar and new sentences, does not hold up: the interpretation depended heavily on her trainers.
- [V46. It's proven that meat played no role in human evolution.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/its-proven-that-meat-played-no-role-in-human-evolution.html): It overstates a real study. Barr and colleagues showed in 2022 that the apparent increase in evidence of meat-eating in the time of *Homo erectus* disappears once research effort is accounted for. That weakens one hypothesis, but it doesn't prove meat played no role.
- [V47. Science proves veganism is right.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/science-proves-veganism-is-right.html): Science answers questions of fact, such as whether animals feel pain and whether a vegan diet can be healthy. Whether it is right to cause that suffering is a moral question, which no study answers on its own.
- [V48. Oysters and mussels feel pain like any other animal.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/oysters-and-mussels-feel-pain-like-any-other-animal.html): The evidence of sentience in bivalves is weak: they have very simple nervous systems with no centralized brain, and even animal advocates admit they may not feel.
- [V49. Cultivated meat isn't vegan, because it comes from animals.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/cultivated-meat-isnt-vegan-because-it-comes-from-animals.html): The definitional objection confuses the letter of the commitment with its spirit: veganism is not a closed list of forbidden ingredients, it is a commitment to ending unnecessary harm to sentient beings.
- [V50. Food that may contain traces of milk isn't vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/food-that-may-contain-traces-of-milk-isnt-vegan.html): "May contain traces" is a warning for people with allergies: the product went through machines that also process that ingredient. The ingredient isn't in the recipe.
- [V51. A good vegan only eats natural, organic, healthy food.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/a-good-vegan-only-eats-natural-organic-healthy-food.html): Nothing in vegan ethics requires that. The concern is not exploiting animals, whether dinner is an organic salad or French fries.
- [V52. On a desert island, I'd starve before eating an animal.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/on-a-desert-island-id-starve-before-eating-an-animal.html): The very definition of veganism speaks of avoiding exploitation "as far as is possible and practicable". In a real survival situation, not eating an animal may be beyond what is possible, and saying otherwise creates a demand veganism does not make.
- [V53. Anyone who supports step-by-step change isn't really vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anyone-who-supports-step-by-step-change-isnt-really-vegan.html): Veganism is defined by refusing animal exploitation as far as is possible and practicable, not by a position on strategy. Someone can be vegan and support gradual reforms, or be vegan and reject them.
- [V54. Anyone who won't accept gradual change doesn't understand how the world works.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anyone-who-wont-accept-gradual-change-doesnt-understand-how-the-world.html): It mirrors the previous item, said by supporters of gradual change against those who call for an immediate end to exploitation. Asking people to stop now isn't naive: it states the goal clearly.
- [V55. Anyone who buys products from big companies isn't vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anyone-who-buys-products-from-big-companies-isnt-vegan.html): Veganism is about the exploitation of animals. A vegan product from a big company involves no animal exploitation in the product itself. Criticisms of big companies can be legitimate, but they are a different discussion.
- [V56. Anyone who supports capitalism isn't really vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anyone-who-supports-capitalism-isnt-really-vegan.html): It is the same mistake as demanding that vegans be anti-capitalist, in the opposite direction: it turns an economic position into a condition for defending animals.
- [V57. I'm vegan, but I taste the food when I visit my family.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/im-vegan-but-i-taste-the-food-when-i-visit-my-family.html): If the reason not to eat animals is the animal, it doesn't change because the table belongs to your family. For whoever died, the occasion makes no difference.
- [V58. I'm vegan, but I don't think everyone should be.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/im-vegan-but-i-dont-think-everyone-should-be.html): It treats as personal taste something that has a victim. No one says "I'm against assaulting people, but I don't think everyone should be." If the harm is unjust when you cause it, it is also unjust when someone else does.
- [V59. I'm vegan, but I have nothing against people who eat meat.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/im-vegan-but-i-have-nothing-against-people-who-eat-meat.html): It is a very common line, said to avoid conflict, and the intention is good: respecting people. But it mixes two things, having nothing against the person and having nothing against what they do.
- [V60. My partner isn't vegan, but we accept our differences.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/my-partner-isnt-vegan-but-we-accept-our-differences.html): Respecting differences is important, and real relationships require care: no one has to break with someone they love over a disagreement, and there is no single formula. It is a controversial question.
- [V61. Being vegan requires being anti-capitalist.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/being-vegan-requires-being-anti-capitalist.html): When someone says this without saying, just as firmly, that anti-capitalists should be vegan, the real goal isn't animal welfare. It's recruiting supporters for another cause from inside the vegan movement.
- [V62. More expensive meat is bad for ordinary people.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/more-expensive-meat-is-bad-for-ordinary-people.html): When the price of animal products rises, the drop in consumption is usually treated only as sad news, and not also as what it is: fewer animals killed.
- [V63. Veganism is only about animals; nothing else matters.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/veganism-is-only-about-animals-nothing-else-matters.html): Veganism does focus on animal exploitation, but that's no license to treat other humans unfairly or with prejudice. Humans are sentient too, and the criterion applies to them.
- [V64. Veganism and environmentalism without class struggle is just gardening.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/veganism-and-environmentalism-without-class-struggle-is-just-gardening.html): The phrase comes from a widely repeated saying, "ecology without class struggle is gardening", often attributed to the Brazilian activist Chico Mendes. Applied to veganism, it mixes two different causes: environmentalism does not presuppose veganism as a moral position. At most, for technical and evidential reasons, it recommends reducing animal farming because of its impact.

## Political objections

- [Liberalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/liberalism.html): Freedom is a right of rational individuals; animals aren't subjects of liberal rights. Protect individuals against harm caused by others and ensure each can live their own life. For the English philosopher John Stuart Mill (1806–1873), one of the leading names of liberalism, the only legitimate reason to limit someone's freedom is to prevent harm to others. This is the harm principle, which he sets out in On Liberty (1859).
- [Libertarianism and anarcho-capitalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/libertarianism.html): What's mine is mine: animals are property, and the freedom to use property is sacred. Self-ownership and the non-aggression principle: no one may initiate violence against another individual.
- [Marxism, socialism and communism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/marxism.html): Exploitation is a relation between human classes. Animals aren't workers, and the struggle is a different one. End exploitation and the turning of beings and lives into commodities.
- [Anarchism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/anarchism.html): Anarchism fights domination between people; animals are not part of that. Reject hierarchies and forms of domination that cannot be justified.
- [Utilitarianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/utilitarianism.html): Human pleasures are worth more: better to be a human dissatisfied than a pig satisfied. Maximize well-being and minimize suffering for everyone affected, counting each one's interest equally.
- [Contractualism and Rawlsian justice](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/contractualism.html): Justice holds among those who have a sense of justice and can make agreements. Choose the rules of a society impartially, as if we did not know what position we would occupy in it.
- [Deontology and Kantianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/deontology.html): Only rational beings are ends in themselves; toward animals we have, at most, indirect duties. Treat beings who have value of their own as ends, and never merely as means.
- [Communitarianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/communitarianism.html): Duties arise from the community and its traditions, and animals are not members of it. Morality is built in the bonds and practices of a community.
- [Egalitarianism and prioritarianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/egalitarianism.html): Equality is among human citizens; animals belong to another category. Reduce unjust inequalities and give priority to those who are worst off.
- [Ethics of care](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/care-ethics.html): Care applies to close relationships, not to unknown animals. Respond to the needs of the vulnerable and the dependent with attention and responsibility.
- [Virtue ethics](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/virtue-ethics.html): Virtue is about human character; treating animals well matters only because it makes us better. Cultivate virtues like compassion, justice and temperance, and avoid vices like cruelty.
- [Feminism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/feminism.html): Feminism is about women; talking about cows and hens is changing the subject, or even offensive. End oppression linked to sex and control over the body and reproduction.
- [Anti-racism and anti-ableism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/anti-discrimination.html): Comparing speciesism to racism or ableism is offensive; they are different things. Do not give less weight to someone's interests because of a trait that does not change how much they can be harmed, such as race, disability, origin or appearance.
- [The progressive left and multiculturalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/progressive-left-and-multiculturalism.html): The animal cause is a white middle-class concern that ends up attacking the cultural practices of minorities. Defend vulnerable groups, fight domination and respect cultural diversity.
- [Pacifism and nonviolence](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/pacifism.html): Nonviolence is a commitment between people, not to animals. Refuse violence as a means of resolving conflicts and reaching goals.
- [Effective altruism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/effective-altruism.html): Resources for doing good are limited, and should go to humans first. Use evidence and reason to do the most good possible with the resources available.
- [Environmentalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/environmentalism.html): What matters is saving the planet, ecosystems and species, not each individual animal. Protect the environment and the planet: conserve ecosystems, biodiversity and natural resources, and secure living conditions for present and future generations.
- [Pragmatism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/pragmatism.html): Politics is the art of the possible: the animal cause is not viable, wins no votes, and there are more practical problems to solve. Judge ideas and policies by their practical consequences, not by loyalty to a doctrine; test, look at the results and correct course.

## Beyond veganism

- [Antispeciesism and sentientism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/antispeciesism.html): Veganism is one consequence of a broader criterion: what matters morally is the capacity to be harmed or benefited.
- [The state of the art in animal ethics](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/state-of-the-art.html): Since 1975, animal ethics has been tested on ever harder cases, by authors from schools that disagree with each other, and has reached the same rejection of speciesism.
- [Wild animal suffering](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/wild-animals.html): Hunger, disease and predation were not caused by us. But if sentience is what matters, this suffering cannot be dismissed just because it is natural.
- [Sentience in AI and robots](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/ai-and-robots.html): No current system is recognized as sentient. But the possibility is not absurd, and the criterion does not depend on what a being is made of.
- [The definition of veganism, debated](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/defining-veganism.html): What defines veganism: refusing the exploitation of animals, or refusing everything of animal origin? The question has come back strongly with cultivated meat and precision fermentation.
- [Sentience in extraterrestrials, plants and other forms of life](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/extraterrestrials.html): There is no evidence of life beyond Earth, let alone sentient life, and no robust evidence that plants or fungi feel. Both questions test whether our criterion is really a criterion, and what we would do if the evidence changed.
- [What supports animal ethics, and what weakens it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/foundations.html): Critical reason, relevance, impartiality and sentience support veganism and animal ethics. Partiality, relativism, tribalism, ableism, making abstractions sacred and weak will weaken them.
- [Restraint with indirect arguments](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/direct-arguments.html): Just as vegans should be careful when criticizing other vegans, those who use health and environment arguments should be careful not to strengthen anthropocentrism and environmentalism, which work against animals.
- [The currents of the vegan movement](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/currents-of-veganism.html): All vegans want the end of animal exploitation. The currents disagree about why, with whom and how to get there. A map of the ends, the means and the main debates.
